claims.text: A StorageClass contains the field provisioner (plus parameters, reclaimPolicy), used when a PersistentVolume of that class is dynamically provisioned to satisfy a PVC; a claim requests a class by naming it in storageClassName.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Storage > Storage Classes > StorageClass objects; refs/kubernetes-website/content/en/docs/concepts/storage/storage-classes.md

claims.text: Dynamic volume provisioning creates storage volumes on demand, so cluster administrators do not have to create them (and their PersistentVolume objects) manually ahead of time.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Storage > Dynamic Volume Provisioning (intro); refs/kubernetes-website/content/en/docs/concepts/storage/dynamic-provisioning.md

claims.text: When a PVC does not specify storageClassName, the default StorageClass is used; a cluster can have no default StorageClass at all.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Storage Classes > Default StorageClass; Persistent Volumes > Class (DefaultStorageClass admission plugin)

claims.text: In the kind cluster donhang (kind v0.33), kubectl get storageclass shows one class, standard (default), provisioner rancher.io/local-path, VOLUMEBINDINGMODE WaitForFirstConsumer (storage-class.txt lines 1-3).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/storage-class.txt lines 1-3; kind.sigs.k8s.io user guide (default storage class)

claims.text: WaitForFirstConsumer delays binding and provisioning of a PersistentVolume until a Pod using the PVC is created; the PV is provisioned conforming to the Pod's scheduling constraints. Before that the claim is Pending with no PV (storage-class.txt line 7).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Storage Classes > Volume binding mode; outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/storage-class.txt lines 5-10

claims.text: With standard, the provisioner creates the volume as a folder under /var/local-path-provisioner/ on the node kube-scheduler chose for writer, and the PV's nodeAffinity names that node (storage-class.txt lines 12-16; storage-class.sh comment lines 28-29).
A PV can specify node affinity limiting which nodes it can be accessed from; Pods that use the PV are only scheduled to nodes selected by that node affinity.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Persistent Volumes > Node Affinity; refs/kubernetes-website/content/en/docs/concepts/storage/persistent-volumes.md line 732

claims.text: kubectl cordon marks a node unschedulable: the scheduler places no new Pods on it; kubectl uncordon makes it schedulable again.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Architecture > Nodes > Manual Node administration (kubectl cordon)

claims.text: With writer's node cordoned, the recreated writer stays Pending; FailedScheduling: 1 node didn't match PV node affinity, 1 had untolerated taints, 1 unschedulable (0/3); after uncordon it runs (storage-class.txt lines 18-32).

Mapping of the three FailedScheduling reasons: the other worker fails node affinity, writer's node is unschedulable, the control-plane node is excluded by its taint (kind's control-plane node is not used for ordinary Pods).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Taints and Tolerations / well-known taint node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane; deploy/k8s/kind-config.yaml (1 control-plane, 2 workers)

claims.text: kind runs each node as a Docker container; deploy/k8s/kind-config.yaml at stage-3 declares one control-plane and two workers and sets no extraMounts, so no host folder is mapped into the nodes.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang deploy/k8s/kind-config.yaml lines 1-14 at stage-3; kind.sigs.k8s.io configuration (extraMounts)

claims.text: A local-path volume's files sit in a folder on one node; with no extraMounts no host folder is mapped to it and no other node holds a copy, so the files depend on that one node (principle only; nothing said about deletion).
claims.source_hint: Follows from claims 6, 11, 13: local-path-provisioner README (volume only accessible on the node where provisioned); deploy/k8s/kind-config.yaml (no extraMounts)

claims.text: Replicated storage (copies on other nodes or outside the cluster) requires a provisioner designed for it; local-path keeps each volume on the one node where it was provisioned, and only that node can access it.
claims.source_hint: local-path-provisioner README (node-local storage); kubernetes.io: Volumes > local (subject to availability of the underlying node)

claims.text: volumeBindingMode Immediate: binding and dynamic provisioning occur once the PVC is created, without knowledge of Pod scheduling; Immediate is the default when the field is unset.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Storage Classes > Volume binding mode

claims.text: deploy/k8s/lessons/data-pvc.yaml at stage-3: PVC data, namespace storage-lessons, ReadWriteOnce, 100Mi, no storageClassName; comment lines 4-5 say the default StorageClass provides it (standard in kind).

storage-class.sh at stage-3: L6 show echoes $ cmd, runs it; 21-22 sleep 5, count PVs; 30-32 Pod node, PV, PV node; 34 class, policy, hostPath or local path; 35 compare; 41-44 cordon, delete, reapply; 48-49 last FailedScheduling event, sed cuts 0/N; 53-56 uncordon.
Which StorageClass is default depends on what was marked default in that cluster (by its administrators, or set by e.g. a cloud provider); different provisioners and binding modes behave differently.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Storage Classes > Default StorageClass ('one hasn't been set for you by, for example, a cloud provider'); Dynamic Volume Provisioning > Defaulting Behavior

claims.text: The Pod reaches kube-scheduler through the API server; kube-scheduler records the chosen node on the PVC (annotation volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node) via the API server; only then does the provisioner create the folder on that node and the PV.
